findings.title: IP assignment timing conflict
findings.deviation: Contractor assigns Work Product only 'effective upon payment', whereas the Harrington contract requires ownership 'from creation'.
findings.impact: AtliQ may be in breach of its client contract if rights haven't vested in AtliQ due to a pending payment at the time Harrington expects ownership.
findings.quote: To the extent any Work Product is not a work made for hire, the Contractor hereby assigns to the Company all right, title and interest in it, including all intellectual property rights, effective upon payment for the Services to which it relates.
findings.counterPosition: Make assignment effective from creation to ensure AtliQ can meet its obligations to Harrington.
findings.linkedQuote: All Deliverables shall be deemed "works made for hire" ... and shall be the sole and exclusive property of Client from creation.

findings.title: Missing HIPAA/BAA flow-down
findings.deviation: The contractor will handle EHR and clinical data, but the contract lacks the BAA and offshore data restrictions required by Harrington.
findings.impact: AtliQ is in breach of Harrington BAA Article 4.3 and faces high regulatory risk by giving a subcontractor access to PHI without a back-to-back BAA.
findings.quote: The Parties have entered into, or will enter into, a Mutual Nondisclosure Agreement, which shall also apply.
findings.counterPosition: Execute a sub-BAA with the Contractor that mirrors the Harrington BAA, including the prohibition on offshore access (Art 4.1).
findings.linkedQuote: Business Associate shall ensure that each Subcontractor agrees in writing, prior to any access to PHI, to the same restrictions, conditions and requirements that apply to Business Associate under this BAA.

findings.title: Missing personnel vetting requirements
findings.deviation: Daniel's contract lacks the background check, drug screening, and immunization training mandated by the client contract.
findings.impact: AtliQ cannot fulfill its personnel-qualification promises to Harrington regarding the clinical analytics project.
findings.quote: The Contractor shall perform the Services in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with generally accepted industry standards, and shall comply with the Company's reasonable instructions regarding deliverables and timelines.
findings.counterPosition: Add a clause requiring the Contractor to complete and pass Harrington’s background check and compliance training prior to starting work.
findings.linkedQuote: Contractor Personnel accessing Client facilities or systems shall complete Client's background check, drug screening, immunization and compliance training requirements.

findings.title: Missing client consent for subcontracting
findings.deviation: The contract requires AtliQ's consent for further subcontracting but doesn't reflect that AtliQ itself needs Harrington's prior written approval for Daniel.
findings.impact: AtliQ may be in material breach of the Harrington MSA by assigning Daniel to the project without the client's formal written sign-off.
findings.quote: The Contractor may not assign or subcontract this Agreement without the Company's prior written consent.
findings.counterPosition: Make Daniel's engagement contingent on Harrington providing written consent as required by Article 2.5 of the MSA.
findings.linkedQuote: Business Associate shall not engage any Subcontractor in connection with the Services without Covered Entity's prior written approval of such Subcontractor.

findings.title: Work starts before client signature
findings.deviation: The Contractor is scheduled to start on October 5, 2026, while the Harrington contract is still in un-marked-up draft status.
findings.impact: AtliQ will incur costs and provide platform access before securing the revenue contract or finalizing the flow-down of liabilities.
findings.quote: October 5, 2026 (or the Effective Date, if later)
findings.counterPosition: Sync the start date with the execution of the Harrington MSA and BAA.

findings.title: Missing general indemnity
findings.deviation: The contract lacks a mutual indemnity clause for breach or negligence, which is the AtliQ standard.
findings.impact: AtliQ has no contractual mechanism to recover from Daniel for third-party claims (e.g. data breach or negligence) other than a basic breach claim.
findings.quote: 9.1 The Contractor warrants that the Work Product will be original... 9.2 Each Party's aggregate liability... shall not exceed the total fees...
findings.counterPosition: Include a mutual indemnity for third-party claims caused by a party's breach or negligence, subject to the liability cap.

fine.note: 30-day payment terms match AtliQ's preferred standard.
The mutual 1x fees cap with appropriate carve-outs for confidentiality and fraud is standard.
14-day mutual notice for convenience is consistent with AtliQ's 15-day freelancer standard.
No liquidated damages are included, avoiding the 'Never accept' daily penalties in Harrington's paper.
The 6-month non-solicit is narrow and specifically allows working for competitors after the term.
